problem_type: Renderer-triggered LAN listener without a single trust boundary
symptom: The director console's mobile virtual camera needs the main process to open a LAN HTTPS + WebSocket listener on the renderer's request. Without one gated entry, any web content in the app could start a listener, and any LAN client could push camera packets into the active project.
direct_cause: A new IPC surface (nomi:director:mobile:start/stop/status + event push) and a new network listener (electron/director/mobileBridgeServer.ts) are introduced by the director console cutover.
class_root: Every renderer-reachable main-process capability that opens a network or OS resource must be bound to a trusted sender and every inbound client must authenticate; the bridge is a new instance of that class.
affected_population: Every director console session that connects a phone
Every LAN peer that can reach the machine while the bridge is running
entry_points: WebSocket handshake of the LAN bridge (token in the pairing URL)
32-byte camera packet decode into the active camera pose
internal_only_reason: The trust boundary (assertTrustedSender on IPC, per-session token on the LAN socket, fixed 32-byte packet contract) is an application contract shared with electron/ipcSenderGuard.ts and src/workbench/generationCanvas/nodes/director/model/mobileCamera.ts; no third-party protocol defines it.
invariants: All three IPC handlers call assertTrustedSender before touching the bridge; untrusted senders never start, stop, or read the listener.
The listener only accepts a WebSocket after a token handshake; a missing or wrong token is rejected and never reaches the packet decoder.
The listener stops when the director editor unmounts (useMobileCamera cleanup) and on app quit; it is never left running without an editor.
Packets are fixed-size Float32 frames decoded by the shared mobileCamera math; malformed sizes are dropped, not applied.
generality_proof: The IPC registration is the only place the bridge server is instantiated, and it goes through the same ipcSenderGuard every other privileged IPC uses; the WebSocket path is the only network entry, gated by the token issued at start. There is no second way to reach the listener from the renderer or the LAN.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the renderer-facing lifecycle (start/stop/status + event push) behind assertTrustedSender; the only owner of the bridge server instance.
Own the LAN listener, token handshake, device registry, and packet decoding; refuses un-authenticated clients before any state changes.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: mobileBridgeServer.test.ts covers rejected handshake without / with wrong token and the event inbox for hello / pong / record.
Preload only forwards to the three named channels; no raw ipcRenderer is exposed.

recurrence.reason: The bridge is a single new listener; the class (trusted-sender IPC + authenticated network entry) is already enforced repo-wide by ipcSenderGuard and check:ipc-sender-binding.
same_class_scan: check:ipc-sender-binding passes with the new handlers.

legacy_paths.rationale: New capability; there is no previous mobile bridge to retire.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The listener uses Node's built-in https / ws stack already present in the app; no new runtime dependency governs the trust boundary.

migration: No persisted data. The self-signed certificate is cached under userData and regenerated if missing.
residual_risks: Real-device pairing (QR scan, certificate trust prompt, gyroscope permission) is verified only with a simulated client in tests and a Playwright phone in the S8 walkthrough; it still needs a physical phone.
WebRTC DataChannel transport remains optional and unimplemented.
